title: Max Points on a Line
crux: Find largest collinear subset of N distinct 2D points.
edgeCases: dx=0 (vertical): float dy/dx undefined, needs sentinel key
(-2,4) and (2,-4): same slope, different hash without sign normalization
coords at ±10^4: dy,dx reach 2*10^4, safe in 32-bit GCD
map not reset per pivot → counts bleed across lines

wrongApproaches.name: atan2 angle
wrongApproaches.reason: same IEEE-754 imprecision as float slope

optimal.name: Per-Pivot GCD-Normalized Slope Hash Map
optimal.keyIdea: For each pivot i, reduce (dy,dx) to every j by GCD into canonical pair, count in local map, answer = localMax+1.
invariants: divide dy,dx by gcd(|dy|,|dx|) before keying
clear map at start of each pivot i
pitfalls: map not reset per pivot → line contamination
sign not normalized → (-1,2) and (1,-2) collide only after rule
off-by-one: answer is localMax+1 not localMax
recognizeBy: Map keyed by int pair or encoded long

alternates.name: O(N^3) Cross-Product Brute Force
alternates.keyIdea: Check all triples (i,j,k) for collinearity via integer cross-product.

alternates.name: Per-Pivot Float Slope Map
alternates.keyIdea: Bucket points per pivot by double dy/dx; vertical lines keyed to infinity.
alternates.whyNotOptimal: IEEE-754 wrong answer on non-integer slopes
